column4: When the leaders they followed see the punishment, they disown their followers and their former ties are severed; this gives the section's chief-and-tail relation its judgment-day reversal.
The followers wish they could return and disown those they followed, just as the leaders disowned them in 2:166; this continues the same account of following a destructive chief.
As communities enter the Fire, each curses the community before it; this extends the section's followers-and-leaders relation into a chain of groups that share the end of their course.
The people follow Pharaoh's command, and the verse says his command was not rightly guided; this directly parallels following the section's self-appointed chief over the sent messenger.
Pharaoh leads his people on the Day of Resurrection to the Fire; the verse states the destination of followers carried by their leader.
The verse says Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide them; this is an explicit counterpart to the section's leader who takes the people after him toward ruin.
The deniers say the messenger is only a human like them and warn that obeying him would make them losers; this repeats the human-following objection voiced by Thamud.
The people tell their messenger he is a human like them and accuse him of lying; this repeats the section's linked rejection of a human envoy and false charge.
The one who follows the Reminder and fears the Most Merciful unseen is promised forgiveness and generous reward; this states the receptive response opposite Thamud's rejection.
Thamud arrogantly rebel against their Lord's command, then the thunderbolt seizes them as they look; this joins refusal of the warning to its immediate consequence.
They cannot stand up or help themselves after the thunderbolt in 51:44; this completes the destruction of the Thamud whose rejection the section depicts.
Believers are commanded to obey God and the Messenger and not turn away while hearing him; this makes the proper response to the Messenger's spoken warning explicit.

Pharaoh's people are drowned after rejecting signs, while the verse says the earlier deniers were seized for their sins (بِذُنُوبِهِمْ); this joins the section's named root ذ ن ب to followers' culpability and ruin.
The moon is darkened immediately before 75:9 joins the sun and moon; this marks the breakdown of the distinct celestial course in which the moon follows the sun.
The sun and moon are joined at the Resurrection, a boundary that reverses the separate, ordered relation pictured by the moon following the sun in 91:2.
Thamud are told to enjoy themselves for a short time before their rebellion in 51:44; this is the warning-and-delay immediately preceding the end of the same people.

The verse orders obedience to God, the Messenger, and those in authority, while disputes are referred back to God and the Messenger; it marks a boundary between delegated authority and the self-appointed chief in the section.
Those who obey God and the Messenger are promised company with the prophets and other blessed ones; this gives a positive end to following the envoy, opposite the followers' ruin in the section.
The verse commands obedience to God and the Messenger, then says the Messenger's duty is only clear delivery if people turn away; it repeats the section's message-carrier detail.
Immediately before 16:36's sending of a messenger to every community, this verse asks whether the messengers have any duty beyond clear delivery; it states the section's delivered-message claim.
The verse says earlier peoples also denied messengers and that the Messenger's duty is only clear delivery; it joins repeated rejection to the section's final delivery detail.
The verse commands obedience to God and the Messenger, then says that if people turn away, the Messenger's duty is only clear delivery; this repeats the section's carrier-and-message claim.

After the communities entering the Fire in 7:38, the earlier ones tell the later ones they have no advantage over them and both face punishment; this adds the shared consequence of the follower chain.
